h1: Kelp Global: three connected sales products on one design system
subtitle: Kelp Global helps sales teams manage leads, track deals and act on insight without switching tools. We designed its product suite: a browser extension, an analytics dashboard and a deals module, built on one shared system.

cta.heading: Building a multi-product SaaS suite?
cta.body: Show us the products and where they disagree. We'll tell you what a shared system would fix first.

sections.heading: Executive summary
sections.answer: Kelp Global's sales reps and managers were piecing together customer intelligence, pipeline health and deal status from a CRM, email, LinkedIn and spreadsheets. Designit designed three connected products, a Chrome extension that brings contact intelligence into the workflow, the Truenorth analytics dashboard and an end-to-end deals module, on one shared design system.
body: What changed is where information lives: inside the rep's workflow instead of in another tab, in one hierarchy from team to deal for managers, and in a pipeline whose health is visible at a glance.

sections.heading: Project facts

sections.heading: The business problem
paras: Weekly sales reviews took hours of manual compilation from spreadsheets, CRM exports and email threads. Deal tracking lived in spreadsheets with unclear stages and dropped handoffs, so managers could not see which deals were at risk until too late.

sections.heading: The user problem
paras: Reps constantly switched between their CRM, email and LinkedIn to gather information about a customer, which cost selling time and led to missed signals. Managers had data but no single view of team performance.

items.title: Workflow shadowing, overlay architecture
items.body: We observed reps at work, then designed an overlay that surfaces intelligence in place, using progressive disclosure for quick lookups and deeper research, tested across browsers.

items.title: Manager interviews, dashboard hierarchy
items.body: A drill-down from team to individual deal, with templates that support different sales methodologies.

items.title: Lifecycle mapping, pipeline design
items.body: Customisable pipeline stages, health scoring and collaboration features that make deal status visible at a glance.

items.title: One design system
items.body: Shared foundations so a user moving between the three products doesn't relearn conventions.

sections.heading: Key lessons
items: Bring information to the workflow. Don't make people go and find it.
Dashboards need a hierarchy. Team level first, then the deal behind the number.
Make pipeline health visible at a glance. Risk found late is risk you can't act on.
Design the suite, not three products. Shared conventions reduce relearning.
